entries.a: Lower the egg into boiling water. About six minutes gives a runny yolk, and ten to twelve minutes makes it hard boiled. Then cool it in cold water.
For long grain white rice, use about two parts water to one part rice, bring it to the boil, then cover and simmer on low for around fifteen minutes. Leave it covered for five more.
Boil pasta in plenty of salted water for eight to twelve minutes, depending on the shape. The packet will tell you the exact time. Taste it a minute early.
Salt in the pasta water seasons the pasta from the inside. It won't change the boiling point noticeably.
Al dente is Italian for to the tooth. It means cooked but still firm when you bite.
Chicken is safe when the thickest part reaches 74 degrees Celsius, or 165 Fahrenheit.
Pork is safe at 63 degrees Celsius, 145 Fahrenheit, then let it rest for a few minutes.
For steak, rare is about 52 degrees Celsius, medium rare 57, medium 63 and well done 71 or more.
There are three teaspoons in a tablespoon.
There are sixteen tablespoons in a US cup.
A US cup is about 240 millilitres.
There are sixteen ounces in a pound.
An ounce is about 28 grams.
A pound is about 454 grams.
Two pints make a quart.
Two US cups make a pint.
A teaspoon is about five millilitres.
Baking soda needs an acid, like buttermilk or lemon, to make things rise. Baking powder already contains the acid.
Yeast is a tiny living fungus that eats sugar and gives off gas, which makes bread rise.
A roux is flour cooked in fat, usually butter, used to thicken sauces and soups.
Umami is the fifth basic taste, savoury and meaty, found in things like mushrooms, tomatoes and parmesan.
There are five basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami.
Simmering is gentle cooking just below boiling, with small bubbles now and then. Boiling is the big rolling bubbles.
Sous vide means cooking food sealed in a bag in a water bath at a precise, low temperature for a long time.
A marinade is a seasoned liquid you soak food in before cooking, for flavour and tenderness.
Resting cooked meat lets the juices settle back in, so it stays moist when you cut it. Five to ten minutes does it.
Onions release a gas that stings your eyes. A sharp knife, a chilled onion, or a quick rinse all help.
Cooked leftovers keep for three to four days in the fridge. Get them in there within two hours of cooking.
Put the egg in a bowl of water. Fresh eggs sink and lie flat, older ones tilt up, and a floating one is bad.
Cut potatoes boil in about fifteen to twenty minutes. Whole ones take longer. They're done when a knife slides in easily.
Boiling water on a tea bag, three to five minutes, then take the bag out. Milk and sugar are between you and your conscience.
Sourdough is bread made with a fermented starter of wild yeast and bacteria, instead of packet yeast.
Gluten is a protein in wheat, barley and rye that makes dough stretchy.
Gordon Ramsay is a Scottish-born chef famous for his restaurants, his TV shows and his temper.
A vegan diet has no animal products at all, including meat, fish, dairy, eggs and honey.
Vegetarians don't eat meat or fish, though many still eat dairy and eggs.
The record holders are bred chillies like Carolina Reaper and Pepper X, measured in millions of Scoville units. Please keep them away from your eyes.
The Scoville scale measures how hot a chilli is. A jalapeño is a few thousand units, and the hottest are over two million.

For brownies, melt 175 grams of butter with 200 grams of dark chocolate. Stir in 250 grams of sugar, then three eggs, then 100 grams of flour and a pinch of salt. Bake in a lined tin at 180 degrees Celsius for twenty to twenty five minutes. They should still wobble slightly in the middle.

For pancakes, whisk 100 grams of flour, two eggs and 300 millilitres of milk into a smooth batter. Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled pan, cook until golden underneath, then flip. Lemon and sugar is the traditional topping.

For scrambled eggs, beat three eggs with a pinch of salt. Melt a knob of butter in a pan on low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly until just set. Take them off while they still look a little wet, because they keep cooking.
For an omelette, beat two or three eggs with salt and pepper. Pour into a hot buttered pan, pull the edges inwards as it sets, add your filling, then fold it over and slide it onto a plate.

For cookies, cream 115 grams of butter with 100 grams of sugar and 100 grams of brown sugar. Beat in an egg, then mix in 190 grams of flour, half a teaspoon of baking soda and a pinch of salt, and fold in chocolate chips. Bake spoonfuls at 180 degrees Celsius for ten to twelve minutes.

For bolognese, fry an onion, a carrot and some garlic, then brown 500 grams of beef mince. Add a tin of tomatoes, a spoonful of tomato puree and herbs, and simmer for at least forty five minutes. Serve over spaghetti with parmesan.
For mashed potato, peel and cut potatoes and boil them in salted water until soft, about twenty minutes. Drain well, then mash with butter and a splash of warm milk, and season with salt and pepper.
For cheese on toast, toast one side of the bread, pile grated cheese on the other side with a dash of Worcestershire sauce, and grill until it bubbles and browns.
For hot chocolate, warm a mug of milk gently, whisk in two spoonfuls of cocoa and a spoonful of sugar, and don't let it boil. Marshmallows are not optional.
For guacamole, mash two ripe avocados with lime juice, salt, finely chopped red onion, coriander and a little chilli. Taste and add more lime.

For pizza dough, mix 500 grams of flour, a teaspoon of salt, a sachet of dried yeast and 300 millilitres of warm water. Knead for ten minutes, let it rise for an hour, then roll it thin, top it and bake as hot as your oven goes, for about ten minutes.
For a mojito, muddle mint leaves with two teaspoons of sugar and the juice of a lime, add 50 millilitres of white rum and ice, top with soda water and stir.
For a margarita, shake 50 millilitres of tequila, 25 of lime juice and 25 of orange liqueur with ice, and strain into a glass with a salted rim.
For an old fashioned, stir a sugar cube with a few dashes of bitters, add 50 millilitres of bourbon and ice, stir until cold and finish with an orange peel.
If you like it fresh, make a mojito. If you like it sharp, a margarita. If you like it strong, an old fashioned. Ask me for the recipe of any of those by name. Please enjoy responsibly, Commander.
For a smoothie, blend a banana, a handful of berries, a cup of milk or yoghurt and a few ice cubes until smooth. Add a spoonful of honey if you want it sweeter.
For a simple tomato sauce, fry two cloves of garlic in olive oil, add a tin of chopped tomatoes, salt, and a pinch of sugar, and simmer for twenty minutes. Finish with fresh basil.
For fried rice, use cold cooked rice. Stir fry some vegetables and garlic in a hot pan, push them aside, scramble an egg, then add the rice and a splash of soy sauce and toss everything together.
